division_answers.answer:
### [THUD] TRANSPORTATION, HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, AND RELATED AGENCIES
Bottom line: No single clean FY2026 division total is available from the direct facts because the funding is split across separate HUD accounts, programs, and set-asides; the largest directly relevant buckets are tenant-based rental assistance and Homeless Assistance Grants.

Key buckets:
- Tenant-based rental assistance: $34,438,557,000 [[num:src_thud_4a3a0d30_b7b3_442e_8ee2_d6e04108d60d_1]] available on October 1, 2025, plus $4,000,000,000 [[num:src_thud_4a3a0d30_b7b3_442e_8ee2_d6e04108d60d_2]] previously appropriated under this heading available on October 1, 2025, plus $4,000,000,000 [[num:src_thud_4a3a0d30_b7b3_442e_8ee2_d6e04108d60d_3]] available on October 1, 2026; of the sums appropriated, $34,957,000,000 [[num:src_thud_4a3a0d30_b7b3_442e_8ee2_d6e04108d60d_4]] is for renewals of expiring section 8 tenant-based annual contributions contracts.
- Homeless Assistance Grants under title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act: $4,417,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e0672ad1_4356_43e9_afad_46ca77ac5d8b_1]], including $290,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e0672ad1_4356_43e9_afad_46ca77ac5d8b_2]] for the emergency solutions grants program and $4,010,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e0672ad1_4356_43e9_afad_46ca77ac5d8b_3]] for the continuum of care program and the rural housing stability assistance programs; within the continuum of care amount, $52,000,000 [[num:src_thud_30c11cda_a780_42f5_95d8_faec5eaf5d5c_1]] is for new rapid re-housing projects and supportive service projects. The Secretary shall also non-competitively renew expiring projects for one 12-month period under the heading “Homeless Assistance Grants” in Public Law 119-04 and section 231 of Public Law 116-94.
- Family and disability rental assistance: $30,000,000 [[num:src_thud_3084b7ac_9e5f_408b_a16f_59c982635cb1_1]] for the family unification program under section 8(x) of the Act, plus $5,000,000 [[num:src_thud_3084b7ac_9e5f_408b_a16f_59c982635cb1_2]] for new incremental voucher assistance for family unification; and $287,000,000 [[num:src_thud_853b7fb5_28ff_4aa9_be82_2ff235743a46_1]] for project rental assistance for persons with disabilities under section 811(b)(3) and supportive services under section 811(b)(1).
- Other affordable-housing and youth-homelessness programs: Choice Neighborhoods Initiative $25,000,000 [[num:src_thud_b029292b_908a_4003_a3a0_26e5e80e32f0_1]] with not less than $12,500,000 [[num:src_thud_b029292b_908a_4003_a3a0_26e5e80e32f0_2]] to public housing agencies; $50,000,000 [[num:src_thud_972b6fe3_c1bf_4d61_9a94_adea5ba8e0d7_1]] for competitive grants under title I of the Act to remove barriers to affordable housing production and preservation; and youth homelessness demonstration projects $107,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e4156bb6_ba90_4d3d_895c_fabbe74b30cd_1]], with up to $25,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e4156bb6_ba90_4d3d_895c_fabbe74b30cd_2]] for youth homelessness system improvement grants and up to $10,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e9ada4e4_1b7e_4403_af35_2e53e7ea4854_2]] for technical assistance.

Local caveat: Do not add the sub-buckets to their parent accounts; several figures are set-asides or suballocations inside larger program totals.

division_answers.answer:
### [INT] DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR, ENVIRONMENT, AND RELATED AGENCIES

Bottom line: No single clean division-wide total is available; FY2026 funding is split across separate EPA remediation/brownfields/Superfund accounts plus related CERCLA/NIH activities.

Key buckets:
- Hazardous Substance Superfund: $282,749,000 [[num:src_int_d632d786_92bc_4a55_9797_b34bbf18c00e_1]] for necessary expenses to carry out CERCLA, including cleanup activities, to remain available until expended.
- CERCLA section 104(k) grants: $98,000,000 [[num:src_int_68c231bc_233c_49a7_9433_ff67261f494c_1]] to carry out section 104(k) of CERCLA, including grants, interagency agreements, and associated program support costs.
- Brownfields-related EPA administration: Environmental Programs and Management receives $3,114,671,000 [[num:src_int_50ecf038_8cf4_4344_8029_44323ef53133_1]], to remain available until September 30, 2027, including administrative costs of the brownfields program under the Small Business Liability Relief and Brownfields Revitalization Act of 2002.
- Leaking underground storage tanks and related remediation: Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund Program: $88,903,000 [[num:src_int_676ecc67_2618_41b8_9ebb_1b1dcf5cd4b1_1]] for necessary expenses to carry out leaking underground storage tank cleanup activities, to remain available until expended; and $2,000,000 [[num:src_int_43a8dd3d_d24d_47a3_afa5_b1919462588e_1]] shall be for grants for remediation of above ground leaking fuel tanks pursuant to Public Law 106-554.
- Other remediation-related grants: $20,000,000 [[num:src_int_d0525cce_f9d7_46d6_a96c_151d49cd886d_1]] for grants to address contamination on lands conveyed under the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act; and $77,100,000 [[num:src_int_afc6affa_54d6_473f_bd96_34bc61a5fe67_1]] for the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences to carry out activities set forth in CERCLA section 311(a) and SARA section 126(g).

Local caveat: The $3,114,671,000 Environmental Programs and Management figure is a broad EPA account total, not a clean brownfields-only total.

division_answers.answer:
### [THUD] TRANSPORTATION, HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, AND RELATED AGENCIES
FY2026 THUD covers local governments through a mix of formula and competitive housing and transportation provisions. It provides formula grants to metropolitan cities, urban counties, units of general local government, and insular areas under title I of the Housing and Community Development Act, and it includes protections for local CDBG eligibility, including a prohibition on terminating a unit of general local government’s metropolitan city status for grant purposes.

It also funds several local-government-facing grant programs and flexibilities: $50,000,000 [[num:src_thud_972b6fe3_c1bf_4d61_9a94_adea5ba8e0d7_1]] for competitive grants to State and local governments and related entities to remove barriers to affordable housing, $25,000,000 [[num:src_thud_f70814d7_3213_4d74_969b_06ce52e722c1_1]] for Choice Neighborhoods, and $10,000,000 [[num:src_thud_76b6982f_0ee0_4851_9b4a_cf54373de9de_1]] for Rural and Tribal Infrastructure Advancement technical assistance, planning, and capacity building for State, local, and Tribal governments. The division also continues non-competitive renewals for expiring Continuum of Care projects, supports local transit funding, and covers local/regional project assistance and community project funding changes affecting local projects.
